newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says no plans for new Cuban sugar-oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia says no plans for new Cuban sugar-oil deal.

text.p: Russia is shipping its crude oil to Cuba in exchange for raw sugar under a three-year barter deal signed last year, and no new contracts are planned, officials at the foreign trade ministry said on Wednesday.
"We have no information about any new deals with Cuba," said a ministry spokeswoman, referring to a market talk in London about a possible new deal.
"The old protocol is in force and is working all right, and no new contracts are planned," said another ministry official who declined to be named.
Under the protocol, Russia was to receive 1.5 million tonnes of raw sugar in 1996-1997, with the amount rising to 1.75 million tonnes in 1998, paying for it with crude oil.
The second official also said there were no plans to sign a separate, similar deal between Cuba and the governmnent of Russia's republic of Tatarstan.
Tatarstan officials said earlier this year they were seeking to buy 500,000 tonnes of raw sugar over an unspecified period in exchange for oil and spare parts for Russian-made heavy trucks.
"We did not discuss such plans. Besides, 500,000 tonnes of raws is a bit too much for Tatarstan," said the official.

The government chose two Russian trading houses, Alfa Eko and Menatep-Impex, to carry out the Russian-Cuban barter deal this year. Alfa Eko officials have said the government has not yet approved the contractors for 1997. --Andrei Khalip, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
